MTDI Studio · MTDI 5.0

Microprocessing Technological Diagnostic Intelligence

Turn anything that produces numbers (sensors, firmware, software, networks, security logs) into channels. MTDI learns their normal environment, proves each one can be trusted, and explains what it sees. Small enough for a Raspberry Pi.

Use MTDI from any AI

Paste this into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or any coding assistant:

Use MTDI 5.0 from https://github.com/vxnishhhhh/mtdi-studio- for my project. Read docs/AI.md in that
repository first and follow it step by step: read the listed files, run `python -m mtdi adopt` on my
repository, map my project to channels with me, write the manifest and any probes or firmware, then
verify with the commands in step 5 and tell me exactly what was and was not verified.
My project: <describe it>.

The repository is built to be read by machines as well as people: llms.txt, docs/AI.md (the procedure), AGENTS.md (the rules), docs/schema/project.schema.json (the manifest), and python -m mtdi describe (every capability as JSON).

What the name means

MicroprocessingRuns where the data is: pure-Python engine, ~15 MB, comfortable on a Raspberry Pi or any small single-board computer
TechnologicalAny field: hardware, firmware, software, computers, networks, cybersecurity
DiagnosticCaptures readings and the evidence about them: presence, freshness, timing, range, noise, detection limits
IntelligenceNVTRA explains what the evidence shows; the system learns its own environment

Five pillars, one core

flowchart TB
  H[Hardware<br/>sensors · boards] --> P
  F[Firmware<br/>KEY=value lines] --> P
  S[Software<br/>probes · programs · host] --> P
  P{{adapters: serial · tcp · http · python · process · system · replay · simulator}}
  P --> V[00 Validation Chamber<br/>presence · freshness · timing · range · LOD/LOQ]
  P --> E[01 Environmental Intelligence<br/>learn · lock · compare]
  V --> C((MTDI core<br/>8 weighted factors))
  E --> C
  C --> N[02 NVTRA<br/>plain-language interpretation]
  C --> I[03 I³<br/>the interface]
  A[04 Aether<br/>purpose · authorship] -.-> I
PillarWhat it does
00Validation ChamberProves each channel is present, fresh, on time and inside its declared range. Detection limits come from measured noise: LOD = 3σ, LOQ = 10σ.
01Environmental IntelligenceLearns each channel's baseline from the real environment with a time-windowed median that refuses excursions. Lock it, save it under a name, compare against it later. Simulated data can never be saved.
02NVTRAUniversal interpretation rules plus each project's own domain rules (written as data). Every explanation says what a pattern suggests and what else could cause it. Answers questions from the live packet only.
03I³Induction · Interference · Intelligence. The interface, generated from the manifest: intro, glass header, scroll openings, orbits, full-screen pillars, live traces. The same components render the website.
04AetherPurpose, persistence and authorship. Non-functional: shown, never scored.
◎CoreEight named, weighted factors per channel (availability, baseline, signal to noise, clipping, timing, transient, axial consensus, correlation). An evidence-quality score you can take apart; not a probability.

Quick start

git clone https://github.com/vxnishhhhh/mtdi-studio- && cd mtdi-studio-
pip install -r requirements.txt

python -m mtdi run projects/host-health                 # real data from the computer you are on
python -m mtdi run projects/inductra-vaion --simulate   # an instrument, no hardware needed
python -m mtdi watch projects/host-health               # the same, in a terminal (works over SSH)
python -m unittest discover tests                       # 29 tests

Open http://127.0.0.1:8050.

AstroTech——Next project, not started

A new project is one manifest: python -m mtdi new <id> here, or python -m mtdi adopt <repo> to build another repository on MTDI from its first commit.

Start a project with everything around it

python -m mtdi create

The wizard asks for a name and description, then optionally:

NeedsDoes
GitHubgh signed in, or GITHUB_TOKENcreates the repository and pushes
VercelVERCEL_TOKEN (+ VERCEL_TEAM_ID)deploys the project's studio under the name you choose
NotionNOTION_TOKEN, NOTION_PARENT_PAGE_IDcreates a project page: channels, pillars, links
MATLAByour browser's MathWorks sign-inwrites a starter script and opens MATLAB Online (or desktop MATLAB with --local)

Tokens are read from the environment only and never written anywhere; a test checks it. Preview with --dry-run. See .env.example.

Two implementations

matlab/+mtdi is an independent MATLAB implementation. mtdi.verify checks that it agrees with python -m mtdi analyze on the same recording, field for field. The test suite runs this check in GNU Octave. It has not yet been run in MATLAB itself.

Command line

Command
run <project> [--simulate] [--headless] [--record f.jsonl]start the studio (interface, or JSON API only)
watch <project>live terminal view
check <project>validate a manifest and print the channel map
new <id> · adopt <repo> · createstart a project here, in another repository, or with the wizard
`publish vercel\notion\matlab <project>`one integration on its own
analyze <project> <recording>batch summary (MATLAB's mtdi.analyze must match it)
packet <project> · parse "<line>" · describeinspect a packet, test a firmware line, list capabilities
site buildbuild the website from the repository

Honest about

  • The score is a heuristic evidence-quality score, not a calibrated probability.
  • Simulated data is labelled at every layer, never recorded, never saved as an environment.
  • The firmware templates and the ultrasonic sketch have not been run on hardware in this repository. Inductra's firmware has, in Inductra.
  • Engine cost was measured on a 2.1 GHz Xeon (≈25 µs per line). The Raspberry Pi figures in the articles are estimates, not measurements.
  • The GitHub, Vercel and Notion integrations are tested against faithful fakes of their APIs, not against the live services.

Repository

mtdi/                 the framework (engine, core, pillars, adapters, studio, site, integrations)
  pillars/            00 validation · 01 environment · 02 nvtra · 03 i3 · 04 aether
projects/             one folder per project, plus _template
firmware/             PROTOCOL.md and firmware templates (Arduino, MicroPython)
matlab/+mtdi/         the independent MATLAB toolbox
docs/                 AI playbook, manifest reference and schema, articles
site/                 website assets (python -m mtdi site build → site/dist)
tests/                29 tests, standard library only

Origin

Created by Vaishnav. MTDI began inside Inductra Vaion, a Raspberry Pi instrument that measures the electromagnetic environment, where it was the layer that decided whether a measurement could be believed. Inductra Vaion remains its own repository. MTDI 5.0 is that layer made universal.
